verdicts.claim: The macOS bundle id io.github.dixonbalsagna.orbcombatex and the app name 'Orb Combat EX' must not be registered or shown on any page before the formal title search, and the id changes with the title before first release.
verdicts.what_is_true: The placeholder id is committed at export_presets.cfg:153 in the public repo. I could not check registration, but no macOS build has been handed out. The title is already on the live / page as 'Orb Combat EX (working title)' and is the /play/ page title. name-screening.md:186-188 allows that until the formal search, which has still not been run.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: n/a (confirmed). The wording 'not shown on any page' makes the live pages look like a breach when name-screening allows them.
verdicts.fix: Keep it as a pre-store Legal checklist item, and align the wording with name-screening's '(working title)' allowance.

verdicts.claim: Art's hybrid picks pass with conditions (a plain ring, no orange-over-blue, h09 folded arms, an aura that does not strobe, steady dummy squares), to be confirmed on the turnarounds.
verdicts.what_is_true: The ring, colour and folded-arms points keep unbuilt art away from a franchise's look, which is Orb's originality direction. The live Protagonist is blue with teal hair and has no orange. The flash points are real but already enforced: the worn aura drops out at most once per 40 ticks (1.5 a second per fighter) and holds steady under Reduce flashing, which is locked on in /play/.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: A Legal store record stays open until turnarounds arrive that Legal may never receive. That adds screening work for points no law requires.
verdicts.fix: Move the ring, colour and pose points to Art's originality checklist under Orb. Leave the aura and dummy flicker points in the flash register, which already enforces them.
verdicts.belongs_to: Orb's creative direction (originality), via Art; flash sub-points to Accessibility/VFX

verdicts.claim: Finisher styles (Open Palm, Held Breath, Both Roads): the offered hand is not a beckon and the raised hand is at shoulder height or lower (h10). The aura rework and the h10 clips were never received.
verdicts.what_is_true: The finisher poses landed in b36f5fe6 on 2026-10-22, after the live pin 257a766c of 2026-10-19, so only private builds have them. The generator already encodes h10: Open Palm one hand at hip height or lower, Both Roads at or below 82. A beckon or a raised hand is a question of looking like a franchise, not of law. The missing clips are a process gap.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Two open Legal rows (RL-159 and RL-167) keep Art and VFX in a screening loop for an originality rule.
verdicts.fix: Move h10 to Animation/Art's originality checklist under Orb's direction. Close RL-167 as a process item.

verdicts.claim: The energy overhaul and four kits pass with conditions: e11-e13, fx08, kit poses, red read by the analyser, the barrage capped at 3 white bursts a second, grab call-outs once per grab, and 29 legalAsks.
verdicts.what_is_true: The kits from 2c954dfa exist only in docs/combat/pending/energy, and docs/* is left out of every export, so no kit data ships. The pose and shape points are originality rules. The flash points are real, but the shipped register already refuses red and grants the barrage one flash of at most 0.5 weight. I did not run an export to check switches; I only confirmed no kit data sits under data/.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: A High-ranked open store record makes parked design paper look like a blocker and ties up repeated Legal screens.
verdicts.fix: Split the record: the flash points go to the flash register (already met), the pose and name points to Orb's originality checklist. Reopen only when kit data lands in data/.
verdicts.belongs_to: Orb's creative direction (originality) / Combat; flash sub-points Accessibility

verdicts.claim: Energy names v2 are clear in-game, but Scrap Jaw is renamed Scrap Pit, 'teeth' is dropped and the alternate Drill Fan is dropped (e14).
verdicts.what_is_true: The renames are applied: the parked kit and Narrative's names use Scrap Pit with no teeth, and neither 'Scrap Jaw' nor 'Drill Fan' remains outside Legal's notes. Legal's own reason for the Scrap Jaw rename is a content-rating concern (a mouth closing on a fighter, ln02). Drill Fan was an originality point. None of this content ships.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: n/a (confirmed). The record still reads 'open' although its name condition has been met.
verdicts.fix: Close the name part of RL-178 as applied, and carry the mouth-imagery point into the pre-store rating questionnaire.

verdicts.claim: Grapple held poses (tied, pinned, carried) need g06-g08 and the hold lint on every tick before they are drawn.
verdicts.what_is_true: The held poses are already drawn: cl1 and cl2 at HEAD, and pair1-3 also in the live pin. anim_check lints laced hands and the forearm-length gap (g06), and g07's vertical pin is set in socket data. I found no separate g08 carry check. The lint was read, not run. No choke, mount or head carry is a rating margin, not a player-safety rule.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: n/a (confirmed). The status 'Open until drawn and linted' is stale.
verdicts.fix: Update the record (drawn; g06 linted, g07 in data, g08 unlinted) and add a carry check if carries ship.

verdicts.claim: Rally links: Ring Hang renamed Ring Hold, held fighters never dangle, a flash cap across the whole rally, stepped flares merge, wrecks are empty, and scoring never reads casualties (mc04).
verdicts.what_is_true: Ring Hold is applied in the parked rally content, and 'Ring Hang' survives only in Legal's notes. The shipped rally scorer (sim/director/rally.gd) reads no casualty, toll, civilian or occupant field. The per-second flash register already caps every tick, so a whole-rally cap adds nothing. 'Never dangle' and 'wrecks empty' are rating margins on parked content.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: n/a (confirmed). Parts that are already applied keep the row open.
verdicts.fix: Close the applied parts and fold the rest into the rating questionnaire for when the rally links ship.

verdicts.claim: Planet and home names pass as in-game names. Avoid 'The Long Way Round' publicly, and run a formal search before any public use (w07).
verdicts.what_is_true: 'The Long Way Round' is in no shipped data or UI and on neither live page. The planet names sit in docs/narrative/pending, and the rule is written down in movegen-banned.json and planet_names.json. Searching a name before it becomes a public product name is ordinary clearance. Legal's screen used only GeoNames and the web.
verdicts.fix: Keep it as a pre-store clearance item for whichever name goes public.

verdicts.claim: Movegen allows 'ball of the foot' as anatomy only, never in a title or beside an energy word, with 'ball' alone banned (n01). The proposals screen (about 330 KB) is not done.
verdicts.what_is_true: The rule exists. The movegen and the 331,275-byte proposals live only under docs/ (pending/movegen and proposals), which is left out of every export, so nothing ships. Banning 'ball' keeps away from a well-known franchise's ball device and energy-ball image. That is Orb's originality direction, not a legal requirement.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: An open Legal store row asks for a generated 330 KB screen with its own brief, which is work no law needs.
verdicts.fix: Move the banned-word list into Combat/Tools' movegen lint under Orb's originality rules, and retire the proposals screen as a Legal item.

verdicts.claim: Beam answers 1: no aim assist toward towns; the AI swats by terrain and buildings, never people; catch and block use one plated forearm; the Cyborg's 'eat it' is refused; Hem Sweep never splits round a body; c09 places give no cover.
verdicts.what_is_true: The page is paper, and Orb has since replaced it with beam-answers-2.md. The swat already ships, in the live pin and at HEAD. Its direction follows a fixed rule (sky, nearest standing building or ground) and reads no people. The sim has no school, hospital or place-of-worship building type, so c09 binds nothing. The forearm, eat-it and Hem Sweep points are originality and tone rules.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: A store record stays open 'until built and the look gate and held-pose lint are read', over design paper that has since been replaced.
verdicts.fix: Move the record to Game Design under Orb's pillar 5 and originality direction. If QA wants it, add a sim test that the swat never reads people.

verdicts.claim: RT power-up: ground and sky count as one mark; 'the sky opens' must change; townspeople stop and look and never flee or get hurt, with no camera shake; pose stills and a 1,050-tick held-pose test come before it goes live.
verdicts.what_is_true: The RT power-up is paper only: no 'sky opens', 'takes notice' or power-up pose code exists in render, sim, data or ui. The disc, light-from-heaven and mark-count points keep away from a well-known franchise scene. The no-flee point follows pillar 5's menace rule, and the camera-shake point is a comfort choice.
proof: git grep in 8d9b98a2 render sim data ui (none)
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: An open store record waits on stills and a 1,050-tick test for a feature nobody has built.
verdicts.fix: Move it to VFX/Animation under Orb's originality direction. If the feature is built, the flash register and the motion options cover the safety side.

verdicts.claim: The Blender exporter add-on may need a GPL-compatible licence header and its own register row instead of the repo default.
verdicts.what_is_true: The basis is right: Blender's licence page says published add-on scripts must use a GPL-compliant licence. But no add-on exists. The committed tree has no bl_info, no 'import bpy' and no Blender file, so the condition is dormant.
external: https://www.blender.org/about/license/ (accessed 2026-11-07): 'requires that such scripts (if published) are being shared under a GPL compliant license'
verdicts.fix: Retire it as an open item and add one line to Tools' new-tool checklist: an add-on gets a GPL header and a register row.

verdicts.claim: The copyright-holder line and store identity are Orb's call. Stores and banks need the legal name, enforcement exposes it, and counsel should advise how the pseudonym 'Orb' relates to the title.
verdicts.what_is_true: The basis checks out. Steam onboarding wants a legal name and a matching bank name, 17 USC 401(b)(3) allows a generally known alternative name in a notice, and a DMCA notice needs a signature, contact details and a perjury statement. No holder is named yet: there is no root LICENSE, the draft LICENSE:3 is a placeholder and both presets leave the copyright field empty. vision.md:71 already records a personal name for the holder row in the public repo (see AC-151).
external: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/gettingstarted/onboarding (accessed 2026-11-07): 'Do not enter an alias or nickname.'
https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/17/401 (accessed 2026-11-07): 'the name of the owner of copyright in the work, or an abbreviation'
https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/17/512 (accessed 2026-11-07): 'under penalty of perjury, that the complaining party is authorized'
verdicts.fix: Keep it as Orb's pre-store decision, with counsel optional.

verdicts.claim: Wholly AI-made parts are probably unprotected in US law, and the consumer Pro plan gives no vendor IP indemnity. Protection rests on the name and the record of Orb's own work, and Anthropic's terms were to be re-checked before the repo went public.
verdicts.what_is_true: The facts hold. The Copyright Office (Part 2, 2025-01-29) says prompts alone are not authorship, and the Supreme Court denied review in Thaler on 2026-03-02. Anthropic's Consumer Terms (effective 2025-10-08) assign outputs 'if any', and the user indemnifies Anthropic, not the reverse. Orb accepted the risk (ADR 0007). Nothing records the pre-public re-check (the file was last edited 2026-09-30), but today's terms match Legal's account.
external: https://www.copyright.gov/newsnet/2025/1060.html (accessed 2026-11-07): 'but not the mere provision of prompts.'
https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms (accessed 2026-11-07): 'we assign to you all of our right, title, and interest—if any—in Outputs'
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: n/a (confirmed; accepted business risk, not player harm).
verdicts.fix: Record the re-check as done 2026-11-07 with the terms unchanged, and keep this as an accepted IP risk, not a safety item.

verdicts.claim: No volunteer translation may be accepted until Legal sets a contribution term, because the game is 'all rights reserved for now'. Translated move names also need Legal's search in each language.
verdicts.what_is_true: The rule is sound. With no licence, a volunteer's translation stays the volunteer's unless they grant it, and Weblate's own post says libre hosting needs an OSI- or FSF-approved licence, so the unsourced Weblate line is right. Nothing is at risk today: the public repo has never had a pull request, and localization/ holds only the pseudo-locale.
external: https://weblate.org/news/archive/weblate-even-more-open-now/ (accessed 2026-11-07; an older post): 'a license approved as libre by OSI or recognized as libre by FSF'
verdicts.fix: Keep it in the l10n plan, and have Legal draft the contribution term when Orb picks a licence.

verdicts.claim: The provenance of the predecessor fan game is unknown, so nothing carries over from it.
verdicts.what_is_true: The predecessor's title appears only in 11 docs files, never in sim, render, ui, data, audio, net, art, tools or the prototype. The first commit (f9ec6ac6) imported docs, agent files and a 1,200-line canvas prototype, with no third-party assets. I could not compare code with the predecessor (its files are not here), so 'nothing carries over' rests on absence, not proof. The public vision.md:74 names that title, which contains a franchise term.
verdicts.fix: Close it as Orb's answer. Optionally take the franchise-bearing title out of public docs, per CLAUDE.md's no-franchise-names rule.

verdicts.claim: No public asset or post links to docs/ep/vision.md or to Legal's screening notes.
verdicts.what_is_true: The rule is kept to the letter: neither live page nor the README links to vision.md or docs/legal. But the repo is public (vision.md:80), so anyone can read both now. vision.md:71 records a personal name as the copyright holder, :1403 a US state of residence, :199 names a web series and :74 a fan game whose title carries a franchise term. A no-link rule cannot protect files that are already published, and git history keeps them.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: n/a (confirmed). The rule gives false comfort that these notes are private.
verdicts.fix: Orb decides whether those personal details should be public. If not, remove them from vision.md (a history rewrite is Orb's call). Replace the no-link rule with 'treat every committed file as public'.
verdicts.belongs_to: Orb's call (privacy), with Legal and EP process

batch_notes: Every record in this slice is a Legal or Accessibility condition. Most of the look and pose conditions (AC-136, 137, 138, 143, 144, 145) apply to parked or paper content and are Orb's originality direction, not law. Their flash sub-points are already enforced by the shipped flash register, with Reduce flashing locked on in /play/.
Several records are stale: their conditions are already applied (AC-139, 140, 141) or guard artefacts that do not exist (AC-146: no Blender add-on).
The one current exposure is AC-151: docs/ep/vision.md is public and holds personal details (lines 71 and 1403). This report does not repeat them.
Cited review-log lines are byte-identical at HEAD and in the working copy. The working copy has uncommitted review-log rows after line 266, which I did not read.

External sources fetched 2026-11-07: blender.org licence page, copyright.gov NewsNet 1060, Anthropic Consumer Terms, Steamworks onboarding, 17 USC 401 and 512 (Cornell LII), and Weblate's libre post. Thaler's cert denial comes from search summaries of the SCOTUSblog docket, not a direct page read.
Not run (per rules): Godot, the anim_check lint and any export. Lints and switch states are traced in code only.
